rule: Current subjects all take the same runs: the last ones in which the current Geode build line ran, up to currentRuns. A historical subject keeps the runs of its own build line, so results from before and after a behavior change never mix.
caveat: Runs differ more than the libraries do: one library's median load moved by a third between two runs a quarter of an hour apart. Compare libraries within one run, and treat differences under one timing step as ties. Request counts don't depend on the run.

suites.name: Load, save and release
suites.description: Each run loads five fresh profiles, saves each, releases each after a change, loads them again and releases them again, with the steps on one key at least 8 seconds apart. Times are seconds from calling the library until its DataStore request finished.

suites.name: Server hops
suites.description: Two Luau Execution tasks at once play the old and the new server. The old server loads a profile, saves 777, waits 8 seconds, then changes it to 888 (999 when it keeps the profile) without saving. Times are seconds from the new server's load call until it has the data.

scenarios.name: Old server releases
scenarios.description: The old server releases when the new one starts loading, the way a server releases when a player leaves for another one.

scenarios.name: Old server keeps it
scenarios.description: The old server never releases on its own. 999 means the library got it to hand the profile over with its last change, 777 means the new server went ahead without it.

suites.name: Throttling
suites.description: A burst of 160 or 161 UpdateAsync calls on throwaway keys uses up the server's request budget, then the library loads, saves and releases one profile back to back. One sample per run.
suites.caveat: Shows how each library behaves behind a queue Roblox drains at its own pace, not how fast it is.

suites.name: Memory per loaded profile
suites.description: After loading and releasing one profile so the library has set itself up, the task reads the Lua heap with collectgarbage("count") every 0.1 s for 5 s, loads twenty fresh profiles with the same data as the other suites and holds them, then reads the heap again. The result is the difference between the lowest readings, divided by the profiles held. The bench's request log is paused meanwhile so it doesn't count. One sample per run.
suites.caveat: Noisy in both directions. A script can't make Luau finish a garbage collection cycle, so garbage left from before the load can make the result high, and a cycle that ends between the two readings can make it low, even below zero. It covers what the library keeps in Lua per profile, not memory the engine holds.

suites.name: Geode edit time
suites.description: Geode only, in Lune against Geode's test universe on the machine that runs the bench, not on a Roblox server. One loaded profile with the same data as the other suites takes batches of 1000 profile:increment("coins") calls, after one batch that isn't counted. Each edit runs through the profile's transaction pipeline and is recorded for the next save, without a DataStore request. One sample per batch.
suites.caveat: Depends on the machine and Lune version, which the run file records. Compare runs on the same machine only.

metrics.name: Time
metrics.description: Seconds per sample. The median, lowest and highest, the samples and how many failed.

metrics.name: DataStore requests
metrics.description: Requests the library sent for the key during the step, retries included, as the bench's stand-in for DataStoreService counted them.

metrics.name: Saw the final save
metrics.description: Hops in which the new server saw 888, the old server's last change.

metrics.name: Value seen
metrics.description: What the new server read, and how often.

metrics.name: Heap per profile
metrics.description: Growth of the Lua heap per loaded profile.

metrics.name: Time per edit
metrics.description: Microseconds per edit, from a batch's time divided by its edits.

requestMethods.description: A GetAsync with DataStoreGetOptions.UseCache set to false

notMeasured.subject: lapis
notMeasured.reason: Lapis sends every DataStore request from a RunService.PostSimulation handler, and in a Luau Execution task PostSimulation, PreSimulation and Stepped never fired while Heartbeat fired about 62 times a second. Measuring it needs a server that steps physics, such as a live game server.
Taking over a crashed server's lock waits for the lock to time out (Geode 300 s, ProfileStore 630 s, ProfileService and Lapis 30 minutes), longer than a five minute task.

notMeasured.subject: datastore2
notMeasured.reason: DataStore2's default OrderedBackups method needs DataStores named per player, which the bench's one allowed DataStore rules out. Only the Standard method ran.

Every run still records it, but the numbers are noise. A script can't make Luau finish a garbage collection cycle, and a cycle that ends between the two heap readings moves the heap by more than twenty profiles take, in either direction. Two runs on the same build gave Geode -0.5 and 4.0 KB per profile, ProfileStore 11.3 and 0.5, DataStore2 10.1 and 21.9, so the order of the libraries flips from one run to the next.

Only Geode's edits are timed. A Geode edit runs through its transaction pipeline, while ProfileStore and ProfileService change a plain table and DataStore2 calls :Update, so per-edit times side by side would compare different work.
Request budgets grow with the player count, and every task here had none.
